title: Compliance Memorandum on Prescription Currency, Applicator Licensing and Re-Entry under Custom Application and Field Services
content:
**(a)** On plans under Custom Application and Field Services that the catalogue marks as requiring one, a current variable-rate prescription is on file before any pass is written, and a prescription is current for the programme's validity period in calendar days from the day it was written. Whether a current prescription stands on file is read from the plan record for the plan the pass would be written against, identified by its plan number, and it is read before the pass is written.

**(b)** A prescription resting on a soil test older than the programme's soil test validity in months is not current whatever its own date.

**(c)** Restricted-use product is applied only under plans the catalogue allows it on and only by an applicator whose licence has been verified for the crop year, and the verification comes from the licence record rather than from the applicator's assurance.

**(d)** The re-entry interval for the product applied is recorded on the work order and the field is closed for the programme's interval in hours from the end of the pass; nobody at the desk shortens it.

**(e)** Where a prescription lapses part way through a season the plan stays live but no further passes are written on prescription operations until a fresh prescription is filed, and passes on flat-rate operations carry on as usual.

## Points of judgement on clauses (a) and (b)

A prescription is judged on two counts, and it must pass both to be current on a plan that requires one.

| The prescription's own date | The soil test it rests on | Whether it is current |
|---|---|---|
| inside the programme's validity period in calendar days | inside the programme's soil test validity in months | current |
| inside the programme's validity period | older than the programme's soil test validity | not current |
| beyond the programme's validity period | inside the programme's soil test validity | not current |
| beyond the programme's validity period | older than the programme's soil test validity | not current |

The second row is the point clause (b) settles: the prescription's own date being inside the validity period does not save it where the soil test beneath it has gone stale.

## Point of judgement on clause (e)

A lapse does not close the plan. The plan stays live; passes on prescription operations stop until a fresh prescription is filed, and passes on flat-rate operations carry on as usual.
